'''Gerd Faltings''' ({{IPA|de|ɡɛʁt ˈfaltɪŋs|lang|De-Gerd Faltings.ogg}}; born 28 July 1954) is a German [[mathematician]] known for his work in [[arithmetic geometry]].<ref name=mactutor>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Faltings}}</ref><ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy |id=18851}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 1986 for his [[Mathematical proof|proof]]s of the [[Mordell conjecture]] and several related [[conjecture]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Autobiography of Gerd Faltings |url=https://www.shawprize.org/autobiography/gerd-faltings/ |website=The Shaw Prize}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Fields Medals 1986 |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986 |website=international math union |access-date=29 September 2025 |archive-date=24 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124060355/https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986 |url-status=live }}</ref> He won the [[Abel Prize]] in 2026 for these achievements.{{r|Abel}}<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howlett |first=Joseph |title=Gerd Faltings, mathematician who proved the Mordell conjecture, wins the Abel Prize at age 71 |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/gerd-faltings-mathematician-who-proved-the-mordell-conjecture-wins-the-abel/ |access-date=2026-03-28 |website=Scientific American |language=en |archive-date=24 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260324085758/https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/gerd-faltings-mathematician-who-proved-the-mordell-conjecture-wins-the-abel/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=2026-03-19 |title=German Mathematician Wins Abel Prize for Number Theory Work |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/19/science/abel-prize-mathematics.html |access-date=2026-03-28 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Education==
Gerd Faltings was born on 28 July 1954 in [[Buer, Germany|Gelsenkirchen-Buer]], [[West Germany]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gerd Falting |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Gerd-Faltings |website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |access-date=21 March 2026 |archive-date=1 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260301042016/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Gerd-Faltings |url-status=live }}</ref> From 1972 to 1978, Faltings studied [[mathematics]] and [[physics]] at the [[University of Münster]]. Interrupted by 15 months of obligatory military service, he received his [[Dr. rer. nat.]] in mathematics in 1978.<ref name=mathgene/><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Faltings |first=Gerd |date=1 June 1978 |title=Über Macaulayfizierung |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01424774 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=de |volume=238 |issue=2 |pages=175–192 |doi=10.1007/BF01424774 |issn=1432-1807 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=3 June 2018 |access-date=18 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180603071157/https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01424774 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gerd Faltings |url=https://www.shawprize.org/autobiography/gerd-faltings/ |access-date=18 January 2025 |website=The Shaw Prize |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Career and research==
In 1981, he obtained the {{lang|la|[[venia legendi]]}} in mathematics from the [[University of Münster]], where he was an [[assistant professor]]. He was a [[professor]] at the [[University of Wuppertal]] from 1982 to 1984<ref name=Zeit>{{cite news |url=http://www.zeit.de/1984/24/genie-ist-fuer-ihn-normal |title=Gerd Faltings: Genie ist für ihn normal |trans-title=Gerd Faltings: For him, genius is the norm |language=de |first=Roland |last=Kirbach |work=[[Die Zeit]] |date=8 June 1984 |access-date=14 May 2013 |archive-date=2 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202115020/https://www.zeit.de/1984/24/genie-ist-fuer-ihn-normal |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Princeton University]] from 1985 to 1994. In the autumn of 1988 and in the [[academic year]] 1992–1993, he was a [[visiting scholar]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/gerd-faltings|title=Gerd Faltings|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019 }}</ref>

He was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 1986<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fields Medals 1986 – Donaldson, Faltings, Freedman Achievements |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986 |access-date=19 March 2026 |website=www.mathunion.org |archive-date=24 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124060355/https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986 |url-status=live }}</ref> for proving the [[Tate conjecture]] for [[Abelian variety|Abelian varieties]] over [[Algebraic number field|number fields]], the [[Faltings' theorem|Shafarevich conjecture]] for Abelian varieties over number fields and the [[Mordell conjecture]],<ref>{{cite journal |author-link=Gerd Faltings| last=Faltings |first=Gerd |year=1983 |title=Endlichkeitssätze für abelsche Varietäten über Zahlkörpern |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=73 |issue=3 |pages=349–366 |doi=10.1007/BF01388432 | bibcode=1983InMat..73..349F | mr=0718935 | trans-title=Finiteness theorems for abelian varieties over number fields | language=de }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Faltings |first=Gerd |year=1984 |title=Erratum: Endlichkeitssätze für abelsche Varietäten über Zahlkörpern |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=75 |issue=2 |pages=381 |doi=10.1007/BF01388572 | mr=0732554 | language=de |doi-access=free }}</ref> which states that any non-singular [[projective curve]] of genus ''g'' > 1 defined over a number field ''K'' contains only finitely many [[Rational point|''K''-rational points]].<ref>{{citation |last=Hazewinkel |first=M. |author-link=Michiel Hazewinkel |page=19 |title=[[Encyclopaedia of Mathematics]]: Monge—Ampère Equation — Rings and Algebras |date=1 December 2013 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-4899-3791-9 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1994, as an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] he gave a talk {{lang|de|Mumford-Stabilität in der algebraischen Geometrie}} ({{lit|Mumford stability in algebraic geometry}}). Extending methods of [[Paul Vojta]], he proved the [[Mordell–Lang conjecture]],<ref name="BarsottiSymposium">{{cite book | editor-last=Cristante | editor-first=Valentino | editor-last2=Messing | editor-first2=William | chapter=The general case of S. Lang’s conjecture | last=Faltings | first=Gerd | title=Barsotti Symposium in Algebraic Geometry | publisher=Academic Press | publication-place=San Diego | date=1994 | isbn=978-0-12-197270-7 | pages=175–182}}</ref> which is a generalization of the Mordell conjecture. Together with [[Gisbert Wüstholz]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Faltings | first1=Gerd | last2=Wüstholz | first2=Gisbert | title= Diophantine approximations on projective spaces | year=1994 | journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]| volume=116 | issue=1 | pages=109–138 | doi= 10.1007/BF01231559 | mr= 1253191| bibcode=1994InMat.116..109F | s2cid=120642283 }}</ref> he re-proved [[Roth's theorem]], for which Roth had been awarded the Fields medal in 1958.{{r|Abelcite}}

He returned to Germany the same year, and from 1994 to 2018, he was a director of the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Mathematik|Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in [[Bonn]].{{r|Abel}} In 1996, he received the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]].{{r|Abel}}

Faltings has been the formal supervisor of over a dozen [[PhD student]]s, including [[Shinichi Mochizuki]],<ref name=shin/> [[Wiesława Nizioł]],<ref name=niz/> and [[Nikolai Durov]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hcm.uni-bonn.de/old/faculty/Faltings/phd-students.html|title=PhD Students of Gerd Faltings|website=www.hcm.uni-bonn.de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719101917/http://www.hcm.uni-bonn.de/old/faculty/Faltings/phd-students.html|archive-date=19 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 19 March 2026, the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] announced Faltings as the winner of the [[Abel Prize]], "for introducing powerful tools in [[arithmetic geometry]] and resolving long-standing [[Diophantine equation|diophantine]] conjectures of [[Mordell conjecture|Mordell]] and [[Mordell–Lang conjecture|Lang]]."{{r|Abel}} He is the first German mathematician to have received both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Castelvecchi |first1=Davide |title=Mathematician who reshaped number theory wins prestigious Abel prize |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-00819-y |access-date=21 March 2026 |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |date=19 March 2026 |doi=10.1038/d41586-026-00819-y |pmid=41857209 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Faltings married Angelika Tschimmel in 1984; she died in 2011.<ref name="n776">{{cite web | title=Gerd Faltings | website=The Shaw Prize | date=16 August 2023 | url=https://www.shawprize.org/autobiography/gerd-faltings/ | access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>
